questions.solution: The error lies in the phrase "go for." The phrase "go for" is often used to express a decision or choice, particularly when selecting something or pursuing a particular option. questions.questionHtml:

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4' i.e. "Ungracious."

Key Points

  • The word "tactful" refers to having or showing skill and sensitivity in dealing with others or with difficult issues.(विनम्र)
  • It implies a considerate and respectful approach, especially in situations where this can avoid causing offense.
  • In contrast, "ungracious" refers to someone who lacks kindness, warmth, or grace. It's a behavior that's often considered rude or unkind.(नमकहराम)

Therefore, the correct sentence is: 'So it would appear that from now on I am going to have to be more ungracious and diplomatic in my meanderings.

Additional Information

  • Let's explain all the options:
    • "Sycophantic" - This means behaving or done in an obsequious way in order to gain advantage. It doesn't serve as an antonym for "tactful" because being tactful doesn't necessarily mean you're trying to gain an advantage.(चापलूस)
    • "Fawning" - This means displaying exaggerated flattery or affection. It's not the antonym of "tactful," because being tactful doesn't necessarily involve flattery or affection.(चापलूस)
    • "Grovelling" - This means acting in an obsequious manner in order to obtain someone's forgiveness or favor. It's also not the antonym of "tactful," because being tactful doesn't involve seeking forgiveness or favor.(विनीत भाव)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. Tomatoes sown around July in the southern states are harvested in October.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

Tomatoes sown around July in the southern states are harvested in October.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1.

The original sentence, "Tomatoes sown around July in the southern states are harvested in October," correctly uses the phrase "sown around July" to indicate the time period when tomatoes are planted. The verb "sown" is the past participle of "sow," which means to plant seeds in the ground. The use of "around" appropriately suggests that the planting occurs approximately or near the month of July, without specifying an exact date. This phrasing is grammatically correct and accurately conveys the intended meaning.

Here's why the other options are not suitable:

  1. "Tomatoes sown under July" - The preposition "under" does not correctly convey the meaning of time around which an action occurs. It typically refers to being in a lower position or being subject to something, making it inappropriate in this context.

  2. "Tomatoes sowing around July" - This option changes the verb form incorrectly. "Sowing" is the present participle form of "sow," implying an ongoing action. However, the original sentence's context requires the use of the past participle "sown" to indicate that the action of planting has been completed.

  3. "Tomatoes sow around July" - This option incorrectly uses the present tense "sow," suggesting that the tomatoes are performing the action themselves, which is not possible. The correct form is "sown," indicating that the tomatoes have been planted.

Therefore, "No substitution required" is the correct choice as the original sentence is grammatically appropriate and conveys the intended meaning clearly and accurately.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'. We had to undergo a great many difficulties.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement'.

We had to undergo a great many difficulties.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'No improvement'.

Key Points

  • There is no error in the underlined part of the given sentence. 
  • Initially, it may seem using the indefinite article a before the phrase great many difficulties is incorrect. 
  • But indefinite articles often precede descriptive adjectives. - 
    • Example - He is a good boy. / What a nice car!

  •  We use a great many + plural noun to mean a large number of something.

  • For example:

    We had to undergo a great many difficulties. (We had to face a lot of problems.)
    She has a great many friends. (She has a lot of friends.)

The other options are incorrect and do not follow the rule of a great many + plural noun.

  • Option 1) changes the order of the adjectives and makes the sentence ungrammatical.
  • Option 2) uses a singular noun instead of a plural noun and makes the sentence ungrammatical.
  • Option 4) omits the article a and makes the sentence unidiomatic.

 

  • Hence, option 3 is the correct answer. 

Correct sentence - We had to undergo a great many difficulties.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’. My doctor knew that I would eventually recover and do the kind of work I would be doing before.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.

My doctor knew that I would eventually recover and do the kind of work I would be doing before.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'had been doing'. 

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
  • The correct answer is Option 4 because the doctor is assuring that the person would recover and would be able to do the work that he had been doing before/for a long time.
  • The past perfect continuous tense (also known as the past perfect progressive tense) shows that an action that started in the past continued up until another time in the past. The past perfect continuous tense is constructed using had been + the verb’s present participle (root + -ing). 
  • And we also know that 'before' used to connect earlier events to the moment of speaking or to a point of time in the past. 
    • Example: I introduced Tom to Olivia last night. They hadn’t met before. (up to that point in the past)
  • Here, in the given question 'before' is used 'to a point of time in the past.' 
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4. 
    ​

Correct Answer: My doctor knew that I would eventually recover and do the kind of word I had been doing before. 

Additional Information

  • The structure of Present Perfect Continuous:
    • Subject+has/have+been+v1+ing+object+since/for+time.  
      • ​Example: Monika has been waiting here for two hours.

  • The most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence is: The year before last year
  • In this case, the phrase "the year before last year" is the most suitable choice because it accurately conveys the meaning that Shirley achieved good grades in the year prior to the year immediately preceding the current one.
  • The rule that applies here is the use of ordinal numbers and the phrase "before last." In English, when referring to a year that is two years prior to the current one, it is common to use the phrase "the year before last year." This structure provides clarity and avoids ambiguity in the chronological sequence of events.
  • Here's a breakdown of the components in the corrected sentence:
    • "The year": This clarifies that we are referring to a specific time period, which is a year.
    • "Before last year": This indicates that we are referring to the year preceding the one immediately before the current year.
    • By using this phrase, we convey that Shirley got very good grades in the specific year prior to the year before the current one.

Corrected sentence: The year before last year, Shirley got very good grades.

  • Hence, had so deteriorated is the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
  • Thus, option 4 is the correct answer. 

Correct sentence - The condition of the house had so deteriorated from lack of maintenance that nobody wanted to purchase it.

Additional Information

  • Was deteriorating is the past continuous tense form. 
  • Was so deteriorated is incorrect.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence and from the given options we understand that the verb distinguish (be an identifying characteristic or mark of) or one of its tense forms need to be used for the underlined part. 
  • Distinguishing can be used as the gerund or present participle form. Using either depends on the main verb in the sentence. Since distinguish is the main verb in the given sentence, option 1 cannot be used. 
  • Distinguishes is the third person present form. It is also used to maintain subject-verb agreement when the subject is singular. But in the given sentence, the subject is plural (good looks). So, it cannot be used. 
  • are distinguish is a phrase where the linking verb is plural and will only go with a plural subject. 
  • Thus, none of the options can substitute the underlined segment of the given sentence.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed select ‘No improvement required’. A need of an hour is to provide employment to the youth of the country.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed select ‘No improvement required’.

A need of an hour is to provide employment to the youth of the country.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'The need of the'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. Hence, the underlined part should be changed.
  • Here, 'The need of the' should be used instead of 'A need of an'.
  • The given sentence is referring to a specific point of time. Hence, we have to use the definite article 'the' here.
    • Example: The dog that bit me ran away.
  • ​“Need of the hour” means at an unspecified point in time (“hour”), there is a thing that everybody wants or must have (“need”). 
  • While an “hour” usually refers to the point of time that’s exactly sixty minutes long, “hour” in this phrase is not the same.
  • Instead, we’re just referring to an unspecified time frame, and there’s no telling when or if that time frame will end.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 4.
     

Correct Sentence: The need of the hour is to provide employment to the youth of the country. 

Hinglish

  • दिया गया वाक्य व्याकरण की दृष्टि से गलत है। अत: रेखांकित भाग को बदल देना चाहिए।
  • यहाँ, 'A need of an' के स्थान पर 'The need of the' का प्रयोग किया जाना चाहिए।
  • दिया गया वाक्य एक विशिष्ट समय की बात कर रहा है। इसलिए, हमें यहां definite article 'the' का उपयोग करना होगा।
    • Example: The dog that bit me ran away.
  • "Need of the hour" का अर्थ है समय में एक अनिर्दिष्ट बिंदु ("hour"), एक ऐसी चीज है जो हर कोई चाहता है या होना चाहिए ("आवश्यकता")।
  • जबकि एक "hour" आमतौर पर उस समय के बिंदु को संदर्भित करता है जो ठीक साठ मिनट लंबा होता है, इस वाक्यांश में "hour" समान नहीं होता है।
  • इसके बजाय, हम केवल एक अनिर्दिष्ट समय सीमा की बात कर रहे हैं, और यह नहीं बताया जा रहा है कि वह समय सीमा कब समाप्त होगी।
  • इसलिए, ऊपर वर्णित बिंदुओं के अनुसार, हम पाते हैं कि सही उत्तर विकल्प 4 है।

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’. It is a story about Mr. and Mrs. Ansari, who had look to rent an apartment in the city.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.

It is a story about Mr. and Mrs. Ansari, who had look to rent an apartment in the city.
questions.solution:
The correct substitution is: were looking to

Key Points

  • Replace "had look to" with "were looking to" to correct the sentence.
  • "Were looking to" is the past continuous tense of the verb "to look." It is used to describe an ongoing action in the past. In this case, the action of looking for an apartment was ongoing in the past.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 4.

  • "is looking to" - This option changes the verb tense from past to present. The sentence would read, "It is a story about Mr. and Mrs. Ansari, who are looking to rent an apartment in the city." This option is not appropriate because the sentence is describing an action that took place in the past, not the present.
  • "No substitution required" - This option suggests that the original underlined segment is grammatically correct and does not require any changes. However, as mentioned earlier, "had look to" is not a correct phrase in English, so this option is not appropriate.
  • "were looking for" - This option changes the verb "to rent" to "to look for." The sentence would read, "It is a story about Mr. and Mrs. Ansari, who were looking for an apartment in the city." This option changes the meaning of the sentence slightly. "Looking for" implies that they were searching for an apartment but hadn't yet found one, whereas "looking to rent" implies that they were actively seeking an apartment to rent.
  • "were looking to" - This option changes the verb tense to the past continuous, which is appropriate for describing an ongoing action in the past. The sentence would read, "It is a story about Mr. and Mrs. Ansari, who were looking to rent an apartment in the city." This option is the most appropriate because it corrects the grammatical error and accurately conveys the intended meaning.

Corrected sentence: It is a story about Mr. and Mrs. Ansari, who were looking to rent an apartment in the city.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. I tried to contact my dentist but her cell phone appeared to have been switched off.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.

I tried to contact my dentist but her cell phone appeared to have been switched off.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1 i.e. No improvement.

  • The underlined part of the sentence is correct and doesn’t have to be substituted with another phrase.
  • Look at the given sentence in this way: I tried to contact my dentist but her cell phone appeared to have been switched off (by her). This sentence is in the passive voice.
    • The active voice of this will be: I tried to contact my dentist but she appears to have switched off her cell phone.
    • The active voice emphasizes the person or agent who performs an action (here it’s the dentist), in short, the “actor.” The passive voice emphasizes the recipient of the action or sometimes the action itself (here it’s the cell phone).
    • Eg: Active voice- The dog chased the ball. Passive voice- The ball was chased by the dog.
  • The verb tense (have + switched off) when the sentence is in the active voice is present perfect tense. 
    • The present perfect tense refers to an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past or began in the past and continued to the present time. 
    • This tense is formed by have/has + the past participle.
    • In the present perfect tense we make passive verb forms by putting has/have + been before the past participle form of the verb. This is what is given in the question- have been + switched off.
    • Eg: Active voice- I have finished (present perfect) the pudding. Passive voice- The pudding has been finished (passive form of present perfect) by me.  
  • The rest of the given options are grammatically incorrect.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'. We might as well watch a film on TV as there’s nothing much to do.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement required'.

We might as well watch a film on TV as there’s nothing much to do.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'No improvement required'.

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically correct.
  • We know that after the modal verb the base form of the verb is used.
  • Here, 'watch' is used which is in the base form.
  • Thus, the correct answer is Option 1.

Correct Sentence: We might as well watch a film on TV as there's nothing much to do. 

Additional Information

  • In the given question, "as well" is an adverbial phrase that is written in-between the auxiliary verb and the main verb. In the sentence, it means "also". Hence, the improvement is not required in the given sentence.

Important Points 

We use might as well or may as well to suggest doing something because there is nothing better to do or because it has some advantage. For example:

  • We might as well watch a film on TV as there’s nothing much to do. (There is no better alternative than watching a film on TV.)
  • You may as well tell me the truth. I’ll find out anyway. (It is better for you to tell me the truth.)

The other options are incorrect and do not make sense in the sentence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. At some point in the past , there were rows of temporary shops that used to display various cooking utensils.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

At some point in the past, there were rows of temporary shops that used to display various cooking utensils.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4 i.e. 'Long ago'.

Key Points

  • "Long ago" encompasses an unspecified but extended period in the past, aligning with the narrative tone of historical recollection in the original sentence.
  • It implies a sense of nostalgia or reflection on practices not commonly observed today, fitting the context of describing old market setups.

Therefore, the corrected sentence is- Long ago, there were rows of temporary shops that used to display various cooking utensils..

Additional Information

  • Option 1) "Once upon a time" - Tends to signal the beginning of fairy tales, making it less suitable for historical or factual contexts.
  • Option 2) "Before now" - While accurate, lacks the depth of historical implication that "Long ago" conveys.
  • Option 3) "In the past few years" - Implies a relatively short, recent timeframe, clashing with the sense of significant historical distance suggested by the question.
